newsitem.title: USA: Hilton sees savings as pivotal in ITT bid.
newsitem.headline: Hilton sees savings as pivotal in ITT bid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach on Monday said the estimated $100 million in estimated cost savings from his company's proposed acquisition of ITT Corp a major factor behind the bid.

When Hilton acquired Bally Entertainment Corp, it gained a a gambling presence in Atlantic City, New Jersey, as well as a group of hotels aimed at middle-income travelers to complement the more upscale Hilton hotels.
But a combination of Hilton and ITT, which also runs high-end hotels, could slash management and labor costs.
"It's economics that compel these things, and we have the opportunity to put together a company that is simply more economical," Bollenbach told Reuters in an interview.
Bollenbach mentioned consolidation of reservations systems and management overhead expenses as two areas for cost cuts.

Moreover, Hilton will likely scale back ITT's $3.0 billion capital spending program for new hotels and casinos in Las Vegas and Atlantic City because if built, the new operations would overlap current plans.

Hilton also will look at shedding ITT's non-core entertainment assets such as MSG Limited Partnership, owner of Madison Square Garden sports arena, an all-sports cable network and professional sports teams New York Knicks basketball team and New York Rangers hockey team.
Bollenbach declined to talk about sale prices for the assets or about specific cost-cutting measures until Hilton has had a chance to take an in-depth look at ITT's books.
But David Wolfe, financial analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, said the entertainment assets would not fetch anything near the roughly $1.0 billion ITT paid for them.
Bollenbach also declined to discuss how high Hilton might raise its $55 per share cash and stock bid if ITT refused to accept the offer.
He did say he hoped ITT Chairman Rand Araskog could find a position in a merged company. He said he had not talked personally to Araskog or other ITT officials about the offer.
Late Monday, ITT issued a statement saying it would take 10 days to review the offer. Bollenbach did say he was "very happy to hear" that ITT was considering the deal.
He said Hilton would ask ITT's board to lift its so-called "poison pill" provisions designed to thwart takeover efforts.
He doubted a rival might come in and outbid Hilton because there are very few companies that could offer ITT the synergies and opportunities for cost savings that Hilton could.
Lastly, he said he saw no problems getting the deal approved with state gambling regulators or the U.S. Justice Department.
